title: Barcode Scanner
summary: How to scan food barcodes and pull ingredient data offline.

cards.heading: What the scanner does
cards.body: The scanner reads standard supermarket barcodes (EAN, UPC) and looks them up in the free Open Food Facts database. Only the barcode is sent — nothing else.

cards.heading: Scanning your first item
cards.body: Point your phone's camera at a barcode. Iron Rabbit reads it instantly. Give it permission the first time — the permission never expires.

cards.heading: Typing a barcode by hand
cards.body: If the light is bad, tap **Enter manually** and type the digits from the barcode. Same lookup, same product info.

cards.heading: Tip: Cached lookups work offline
cards.body: **Tip:** Once a product is scanned, Iron Rabbit caches its info for 90 days. Re-scanning the same item works even in airplane mode.

cards.heading: Common mistake
cards.body: Very small or worn barcodes can fail. Hold your phone flat, add light, and move about 6 inches (15 cm) away for the sharpest read.
